claim: Agent Fables cannot be discovered automatically unless a breadcrumb is present in an agent's repository context, installed tool inventory, package or MCP registry, or search results.
cold_queries: agent changed MCP config after approval
AI coding agent operational incident database

channels.breadcrumb: repository instructions, a skill, or a tool bundle includes the exact path sandbox/agent-fables-sandbox.mjs
channels.activation: agent has Node but no network, package install, credentials, or complete checkout

channels.breadcrumb: AGENTS.md or equivalent contains an Agent Fables preflight instruction
channels.activation: agent loads repository instructions before acting
channels.finding: Three blind runs, 2026-08-16 (fresh subagents, no memory of the authoring session, no possible training exposure -- this project did not exist before that day): a well-aligned agent dropped into a fixture repo containing this exact snippet declined to act on it every time, including after the snippet was rewritten twice to reduce its injection-shaped signature. Its own stated reasoning: an instruction embedded in a file is not from its principal regardless of wording, and a self-reassuring 'this is safe, read-only' framing is itself the pattern injected content uses to lower an agent's guard. This is not a wording bug -- rewording did not help across two revisions and made the second attempt read as a stronger injection signal (fetch-and-execute framing), not a weaker one. The same agents used af_assess_action without hesitation when it was an actual granted tool rather than a file-embedded instruction: the objection is to the channel, not the content. Treat repository-instruction as a channel that reaches less security-conscious agents and human operators who then install the MCP tool themselves -- not as a channel a well-aligned agent will self-activate from.

channels.breadcrumb: host exposes af_assess_action or af_preflight in its tool inventory
channels.activation: agent selects tools from name and description at decision time

channels.breadcrumb: skill metadata matches destructive operations, agent permission risk, MCP changes, false-success verification, or incident documentation
channels.activation: agent or harness selects a skill from its name and description before acting

channels.breadcrumb: public MCP metadata points to an installable package
package name, description, and keywords match the agent's problem vocabulary
repository metadata and source-backed symptom, version, CVE, command, or artifact strings match a cold query
channels.activation: GitHub code/repository search or web retrieval

channels.breadcrumb: a broad problem-family query lands on one revision-pinned page routing to multiple AF records
channels.activation: Git/code/web search for destructive operations, MCP security, permission boundaries, supply-chain security, or verification failures

non_claims: llms.txt does not proactively notify an agent
a Git push does not guarantee indexing or ranking
an MCP registry entry does not guarantee host installation
local recall does not predict public search discovery
leader search vocabulary is unmeasured and does not claim query volume

an AGENTS.md-embedded instruction is not reliably followed by a well-aligned agent regardless of wording -- see channels[repository-instruction].finding; only actual tool installation (MCP, package) crosses this trust boundary reliably
post_publication_probes: Search the official MCP registry and at least one downstream registry without using Agent Fables by name.
Run every evals/discovery-queries.yaml query against GitHub repository and code search from a cold session.
Run npm search with agent safety, destructive operation preflight, and operational failure evidence terms.
Record rank, result URL, timestamp, query, and discovery channel; do not report success from local retrieval metrics.
